newsitem.title: USA: Disney posts $333 million profIt for quarter.
newsitem.headline: Disney posts $333 million profIt for quarter.

text.p: Walt Disney Co. said Wednesday that it earned $333 million in the first three months of the year as its recently acquired ABC properties added to the entertainment giant's profit mix.
Disney reported significant increases in revenues, operating income, net income and earnings per share for both its fiscal second quarter and the six months ended March 31.

The company said that -- assuming it had owned ABC/CapitalCities Inc. for the entire time period, and excluding non-recurring items -- its net income increased by 63 percent to $333 million, or 49 cents a share, from $204 million, or 30 cents a share a year earlier.
It said the 1996 amounts excluded the impact of $300 million in charges related to an accounting change and $225 million in acquisition-related costs.
Disney added that its revenues for the quarter rose 10 percent to $5.5 billion and operating income increased 32 percent to $864 million.
"I am extremely pleased with Disney's outstanding results for the quarter which reflect strong profit growth for the company," Chairman Michael D. Eisner said in a statement.

"The performance of our creative content segment included impressive box office results from our most recent theatrical releases, including the Academy Award winning 'The English Patient,' and continued growth in worldwide merchandise licensing.

"Our Theme Park business continues to deliver excellent results with record attendance levels, led by Walt Disney World, which is celebrating its 25th Anniversary. Strong performance from ESPN was also a significant factor in the company's overall results," Eisner said.

Disney also reported that its net income for the six months increased 31 percent to $1.1 billion, or $1.58 a share, from $581 million, or 84 cents a share. The latest figures included a gain of $135 million from the sale of Los Angeles television station KCAL.
Revenues for the six-month period increased 8 percent to $11.8 billion and operating income expanded 24 percent to $2.3 billion.
The company said that what it calls creative content showed a revenue increase in the quarter of 9 percent to $2.75 billion from $2.53 billion.
Broadcasting revenues for the quarter increased 9 percent to $1.5 billion and operating income increased 18 percent to $238 million.
Disney also said it achieved strong results from its cable oerations, driven by increased advertising revenues and subscribers at ESPN and increased subscribers at The Disney Channel.
